subproblem.title: Smooth cutoff equal to 1 near a compact set, supported in an open set
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ and all sets K, N ⊆ ℝ^P with K compact, N open and K ⊆ N, there exist a C¹ function ζ : ℝ^P → ℝ with compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ N, and an open set V ⊆ ℝ^P with K ⊆ V such that ζ(y) = 1 for every y ∈ V.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (K N : Set (Euclid P)), IsCompact K → IsOpen N → K ⊆ N → ∃ ζ : Euclid P → ℝ, ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ ∧ HasCompactSupport ζ ∧ tsupport ζ ⊆ N ∧ ∃ V : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen V ∧ K ⊆ V ∧ ∀ y ∈ V, ζ y = 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 3 (the compact set K₀ and the cutoff ζ ≡ 1 near K₀ with compact support inside N), stated for an arbitrary compact K ⊆ N; the parent applies it to K₀ = {tγ(α) : t ∈ tsupport λ, α ∈ tsupport φ}. Euclid P is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, hence a proper metric space.
1. (Margin.) K is compact, N is open and K ⊆ N, so IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open gives δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ N.
2. (Nested neighbourhoods.) Put S := thickening (δ/2) K and C := cthickening (δ/4) K. S is open (isOpen_thickening) and C is closed (isClosed_cthickening). Since 0 < δ/2 and δ/4 < δ/2, cthickening_subset_thickening' gives C ⊆ S.
3. (Smooth Urysohn function.) Apply exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (Euclid P is a finite-dimensional real normed space) with n := 1 to the open set S and the closed set C ⊆ S. It yields ζ : Euclid P → ℝ with ContDiff ℝ ((1 : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) ζ, which is ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ (the coercion of 1 is 1, e.g. by exact_mod_cast), range ζ ⊆ [0, 1], support ζ = S, and, for every y, y ∈ C ↔ ζ y = 1.
4. (Support.) tsupport ζ = closure (support ζ) = closure S ⊆ cthickening (δ/2) K, by closure_thickening_subset_cthickening.
5. (Compact support.) cthickening (δ/2) K is compact (IsCompact.cthickening, Euclid P being proper) and tsupport ζ is closed (isClosed_tsupport); by step 4 and IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset, tsupport ζ is compact, i.e. HasCompactSupport ζ.
6. (Support inside N.) Since δ/2 ≤ δ, cthickening_mono and step 1 give cthickening (δ/2) K ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ N; with step 4, tsupport ζ ⊆ N.
7. (Plateau.) Let V := thickening (δ/4) K. V is open (isOpen_thickening); K ⊆ V by self_subset_thickening because δ/4 > 0; and V ⊆ cthickening (δ/4) K = C by thickening_subset_cthickening. Hence ζ y = 1 for every y ∈ V, by step 3.
8. (Conclusion.) ζ (steps 3, 5, 6) and V (step 7) have all the required properties. The case K = ∅ needs no separate treatment: then S = C = V = ∅ and ζ = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: Choose δ > 0 with cthickening δ K ⊆ N (IsCompact.exists_cthickening_subset_open).

exists_contDiff_support_eq_eq_one_iff (n := 1) for the open set thickening (δ/2) K and the closed set cthickening (δ/4) K ⊆ thickening (δ/2) K gives a C¹ ζ with support ζ = thickening (δ/2) K and ζ = 1 exactly on cthickening (δ/4) K.
tsupport ζ ⊆ cthickening (δ/2) K ⊆ cthickening δ K ⊆ N, a closed subset of a compact set, so ζ has compact support and tsupport ζ ⊆ N.
V := thickening (δ/4) K is open, contains K, and lies in cthickening (δ/4) K, where ζ = 1.

audit.reason: The one-line proposition exactly matches all prose hypotheses and conclusions. The positive compact-set margin, nested thickenings and smooth Urysohn function give the required plateau and support. Properness makes the containing closed thickening compact. The empty-set case is valid. This is a complete, independent proof of the cutoff needed by the parent.

subproblem.title: C¹ regularity and tangential derivative of the angle–radius profile φ(arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩))·λ(‖y‖)
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all u, e, x ∈ ℝ^P with ⟨x,u⟩ > 0, and all C¹ functions φ, λ : ℝ → ℝ, the function F : ℝ^P → ℝ, F(y) := φ(arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩))·λ(‖y‖), is C¹ at x, and for every h ∈ ℝ^P with ⟨x,h⟩ = 0 its Fréchet derivative satisfies DF(x)h = φ′(arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩))·λ(‖x‖)·(⟨x,u⟩⟨h,e⟩ − ⟨x,e⟩⟨h,u⟩)/(⟨x,u⟩² + ⟨x,e⟩²), where φ′ is the derivative of φ.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (u e x : Euclid P) (φ lam : ℝ → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 φ → ContDiff ℝ 1 lam → 0 < inner ℝ x u → ContDiffAt ℝ 1 (fun y : Euclid P => φ (Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y u)) * lam ‖y‖) x ∧ ∀ h : Euclid P, inner ℝ x h = 0 → fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => φ (Real.arctan (inner ℝ y e / inner ℝ y u)) * lam ‖y‖) x h = deriv φ (Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x u)) * lam ‖x‖ * ((inner ℝ x u * inner ℝ h e - inner ℝ x e * inner ℝ h u) / (inner ℝ x u ^ 2 + inner ℝ x e ^ 2))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, step 1 (Df(x)h = (⟨h,e⟩⟨x,u⟩ − ⟨x,e⟩⟨h,u⟩)/q(x) for the angle f(y) = arctan(⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩), via Real.hasDerivAt_arctan and the quotient rule, and the derivative h ↦ ⟨x,h⟩/‖x‖ of the norm at x ≠ 0, via (hasFDerivAt_id x).norm_sq, HasFDerivAt.sqrt and Real.sqrt_sq) and step 6(iii) (the chain and product rule for y ↦ φ(f(y))·λ(‖y‖) in a direction orthogonal to x), stated at an arbitrary point x with ⟨x,u⟩ > 0. No orthonormality of u, e is needed.
Notation: a := ⟨x,u⟩, b := ⟨x,e⟩, q(y) := ⟨y,e⟩/⟨y,u⟩, f(y) := arctan(q(y)), F(y) := φ(f(y))·λ(‖y‖), φ′ := deriv φ, λ′ := deriv λ; "D" is the Fréchet derivative (HasFDerivAt / fderiv).
1. (Nondegeneracy.) a > 0, so a ≠ 0; and x ≠ 0, since x = 0 would give a = ⟨0,u⟩ = 0. Also a² + b² ≥ a² > 0.
2. (Linear coordinates.) For every z ∈ Euclid P the function y ↦ ⟨y,z⟩ equals, by real_inner_comm, the continuous linear functional innerSL ℝ z (y ↦ ⟨z,y⟩); hence it has derivative innerSL ℝ z at x, i.e. h ↦ ⟨z,h⟩ = ⟨h,z⟩.
3. (Quotient.) By the chain rule (HasDerivAt.comp_hasFDerivAt) with hasDerivAt_inv at a ≠ 0, y ↦ ⟨y,u⟩⁻¹ has derivative h ↦ −(a²)⁻¹⟨h,u⟩ at x. Writing q(y) = ⟨y,e⟩·⟨y,u⟩⁻¹ (div_eq_mul_inv), the product rule (HasFDerivAt.fun_mul) shows that q has derivative q′ at x with q′h = b·(−(a²)⁻¹⟨h,u⟩) + a⁻¹⟨h,e⟩.
4. (Angle and outer profile.) By HasFDerivAt.arctan, f has derivative f′ := (1/(1 + (b/a)²))·q′ at x. φ is C¹, hence differentiable at f(x), so by the chain rule y ↦ φ(f(y)) has derivative h ↦ φ′(f(x))·f′h at x.
5. (Norm and radial profile.) y ↦ ‖y‖² has derivative 2·innerSL ℝ x at x (hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq), and ‖x‖² ≠ 0 by step 1. By HasFDerivAt.sqrt, y ↦ √(‖y‖²) has derivative N′ := (1/(2√(‖x‖²)))·(2·innerSL ℝ x) at x; since √(‖y‖²) = ‖y‖ for all y (Real.sqrt_sq with norm_nonneg), y ↦ ‖y‖ has derivative N′ at x, and N′h = (1/(2√(‖x‖²)))·2⟨x,h⟩. λ is C¹, hence differentiable at ‖x‖, so y ↦ λ(‖y‖) has derivative h ↦ λ′(‖x‖)·N′h at x.
6. (Product rule.) By HasFDerivAt.fun_mul applied to steps 4 and 5, F has derivative h ↦ φ(f(x))·(λ′(‖x‖)·N′h) + λ(‖x‖)·(φ′(f(x))·f′h) at x; hence fderiv ℝ F x is this map (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
7. (Orthogonal directions.) Let ⟨x,h⟩ = 0. Then N′h = 0, so fderiv ℝ F x h = λ(‖x‖)·φ′(f(x))·(1/(1 + (b/a)²))·(a⁻¹⟨h,e⟩ − b(a²)⁻¹⟨h,u⟩). Since 1/(1 + (b/a)²) = a²/(a² + b²) and a ≠ 0, a² + b² ≠ 0, clearing denominators (field_simp, then ring) gives fderiv ℝ F x h = φ′(f(x))·λ(‖x‖)·(a⟨h,e⟩ − b⟨h,u⟩)/(a² + b²), where f(x) = arctan(⟨x,e⟩/⟨x,u⟩). This is the claimed formula.
8. (C¹ at x.) q is C¹ at x as a quotient of C¹ functions with nonvanishing denominator (ContDiffAt.div with a ≠ 0, the numerator and denominator being contDiffAt_id.inner ℝ contDiffAt_const); arctan is C^∞ (Real.contDiff_arctan) and φ is C¹, so y ↦ φ(f(y)) is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.comp). The norm is C¹ at x ≠ 0 (contDiffAt_norm) and λ is C¹, so y ↦ λ(‖y‖) is C¹ at x. Hence F is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.mul). Steps 7 and 8 prove the statement. ∎
proof_key_steps: y ↦ ⟨y,z⟩ is the linear functional innerSL ℝ z; with hasDerivAt_inv and the product rule, q = ⟨·,e⟩/⟨·,u⟩ has derivative q′h = a⁻¹⟨h,e⟩ − b(a²)⁻¹⟨h,u⟩ at x (a = ⟨x,u⟩ ≠ 0, b = ⟨x,e⟩).
HasFDerivAt.arctan and the chain rule give D(φ∘f)(x)h = φ′(f(x))·(1/(1 + (b/a)²))·q′h.
‖y‖ = √(‖y‖²), hasStrictFDerivAt_norm_sq and HasFDerivAt.sqrt give D‖·‖(x)h = (1/(2√(‖x‖²)))·2⟨x,h⟩, which vanishes when ⟨x,h⟩ = 0.
Product rule, then field_simp/ring: DF(x)h = φ′(f(x))·λ(‖x‖)·(a⟨h,e⟩ − b⟨h,u⟩)/(a² + b²) for ⟨x,h⟩ = 0.
C¹ at x from ContDiffAt.div, Real.contDiff_arctan, contDiffAt_norm (x ≠ 0), ContDiffAt.comp and ContDiffAt.mul.

The inverse, arctangent, square-root, chain and product rules produce the stated derivative; orthogonality removes the radial term. C¹ regularity is separately established. No orthonormality assumption or circular reliance is hidden.

subproblem.title: Tangential divergence of the rotation field g·(⟨y,u⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩u) on a plane through the radial direction
subproblem.statement: For every P ∈ ℕ, all u, e, v, w ∈ ℝ^P such that (v, w) is orthonormal, every linear subspace Q ⊆ ℝ^P with Q = span{v, w}, every function g : ℝ^P → ℝ and every t ∈ ℝ such that g is differentiable at t·v, the vector field X(y) := g(y)·(⟨y,u⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩u) satisfies tr(P_Q ∘ DX(tv)) = Dg(tv)w · t·(⟨v,u⟩⟨w,e⟩ − ⟨v,e⟩⟨w,u⟩), where P_Q is the orthogonal projection onto Q and DX(tv), Dg(tv) are the Fréchet derivatives at tv.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (u e v w : Euclid P) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (g : Euclid P → ℝ) (t : ℝ), Orthonormal ℝ ![v, w] → Submodule.span ℝ (Set.range ![v, w]) = Q → DifferentiableAt ℝ g (t • v) → LinearMap.trace ℝ (Euclid P) (Q.starProjection.toLinearMap ∘ₗ (fderiv ℝ (fun y : Euclid P => g y • (inner ℝ y u • e - inner ℝ y e • u)) (t • v)).toLinearMap) = fderiv ℝ g (t • v) w * (t * (inner ℝ v u * inner ℝ w e - inner ℝ v e * inner ℝ w u))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: parent proof, steps 4–5 (DX(x)h = (Dg(x)h)·Ax + g(x)·Ah for X = g·A, and the trace in the orthonormal frame via the accepted lemma, using that A is skew and that x is a multiple of the first frame vector), stated for an arbitrary function g differentiable at x := t·v and an arbitrary orthonormal pair (v, w); u and e need not be orthonormal. The frame formula is sibling frame_sum, i.e. the accepted theorem Submission.fvmb_trace_starProjection_comp_eq_sum_inner.
1. (The linear map A.) Let A : Euclid P →L[ℝ] Euclid P be the continuous linear map (innerSL ℝ u).smulRight e − (innerSL ℝ e).smulRight u. By real_inner_comm, A y = ⟨y,u⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩u for every y, so the field is X = fun y => g y • A y.
2. (Derivative of X.) Put x := t • v. g is differentiable at x, and the continuous linear map A has derivative A at x. By the product rule for scalar multiplication (HasFDerivAt.smul), X has derivative g(x)·A + (fderiv ℝ g x).smulRight (A x) at x, i.e. DX(x)h = g(x)·A h + (Dg(x)h)·A x; hence fderiv ℝ X x equals this continuous linear map (HasFDerivAt.fderiv).
3. (Frame formula.) By sibling frame_sum (Submission.fvmb_trace_starProjection_comp_eq_sum_inner) with n := 2, τ := ![v, w] (orthonormal by hypothesis, with span Q by hypothesis) and B := fderiv ℝ X x: tr(P_Q ∘ DX(x)) = Σ_{a : Fin 2} ⟨τ a, DX(x)(τ a)⟩ = ⟨v, DX(x)v⟩ + ⟨w, DX(x)w⟩ (Fin.sum_univ_two, Matrix.cons_val_zero, Matrix.cons_val_one).
4. (Skewness.) For all y, z: ⟨z, A y⟩ = ⟨y,u⟩⟨z,e⟩ − ⟨y,e⟩⟨z,u⟩ (inner_sub_right, real_inner_smul_right); in particular ⟨z, A z⟩ = 0. Moreover ⟨x,u⟩ = t⟨v,u⟩ and ⟨x,e⟩ = t⟨v,e⟩ (real_inner_smul_left).
5. (The two diagonal entries.) By steps 2 and 4,
 ⟨v, DX(x)v⟩ = g(x)(⟨v,u⟩⟨v,e⟩ − ⟨v,e⟩⟨v,u⟩) + (Dg(x)v)·(t⟨v,u⟩⟨v,e⟩ − t⟨v,e⟩⟨v,u⟩) = 0,
 ⟨w, DX(x)w⟩ = g(x)(⟨w,u⟩⟨w,e⟩ − ⟨w,e⟩⟨w,u⟩) + (Dg(x)w)·(t⟨v,u⟩⟨w,e⟩ − t⟨v,e⟩⟨w,u⟩) = (Dg(x)w)·t(⟨v,u⟩⟨w,e⟩ − ⟨v,e⟩⟨w,u⟩).
 (After expanding with ContinuousLinearMap add/smul/smulRight application, inner_add_right, inner_sub_right, real_inner_smul_left and real_inner_smul_right, the required equality is a polynomial identity, closed by ring.)
6. (Conclusion.) Adding the two entries of step 5 in step 3 gives tr(P_Q ∘ DX(t v)) = Dg(t v)w · (t·(⟨v,u⟩⟨w,e⟩ − ⟨v,e⟩⟨w,u⟩)). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write X = g·A with the continuous linear map A = (innerSL ℝ u).smulRight e − (innerSL ℝ e).smulRight u, A y = ⟨y,u⟩e − ⟨y,e⟩u.
Sibling frame_sum (accepted fvmb_trace_starProjection_comp_eq_sum_inner) with τ = ![v, w]: tr(P_Q ∘ DX(tv)) = ⟨v, DX(tv)v⟩ + ⟨w, DX(tv)w⟩.
Skewness ⟨z, Az⟩ = 0 and A(tv) = t·Av leave only (Dg(tv)w)·t(⟨v,u⟩⟨w,e⟩ − ⟨v,e⟩⟨w,u⟩) (expand inner products; ring).

audit.reason: The prose and one-line type agree, including differentiability only at t • v and arbitrary u, e and t. The scalar-product derivative and declared frame_sum dependency give the two diagonal terms. Skewness cancels both g terms and the radial derivative term, leaving exactly the claimed expression. The frame literal has the intended Fin 2 family type. The proof is complete and non-circular.
